issues.failure_explanation: For n<\widetilde n, f_n lies in V_{\widetilde n}, so \sigma_{\widetilde n}(f_n)=0 and the chain \sigma_{\widetilde n}(f_n)\ge\sigma_{\widetilde n+1}(f_{\widetilde n+1}) is false. The claim itself fails. Interior batch elements are selected with the stale surrogate r_{\undertilde n}, or arbitrarily by Remark (c), and may be (nearly) dependent on earlier batch members. Counterexample: \cF={3^{-k}(1-j/(2b))e_k}, \gamma=1, exact surrogate. Each batch consists of b multiples of a single e_k, so a_{n,n}=0 for interior n while \sigma_{n+b-1}>0. Then \sigma_{b\ell}=3^{-\ell-1}, whereas col:wbg_hilbert(i) would force \sigma_{2n+b-1}\le\sqrt2 d_n^{1/2}\approx 3^{-n/2}, which is violated for b\ge5 and large \ell. The Banach lemma repeats the same unjustified step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must impose a selection condition on every batch element guaranteeing dist(f_n,V_n) \gtrsim \sigma_{n+c(b)} (not available from r_{\undertilde n} without new snapshots). Alternatively, the analysis must be redone using only the first element of each batch, which yields rates in terms of n/b.
issues.overall_effect: All convergence rates claimed for Algorithm alg:wbg, in both Hilbert and Banach settings, are unproven and in general false for the algorithm as stated. This includes the asymptotic-loss quantification and the abstract's claim to have proved convergence rates.

issues.failure_explanation: In (ii), the first-violation argument is an induction with a single constant: it uses \sigma_{2s}\le C_1(2s)^{-\alpha}. It reaches a contradiction only if C_1\ge 2^{\alpha+1}\gamma^{-2}\lceil4+(b-1)/s\rceil^{2\alpha}C_0, where s<M is the auxiliary index, not n=M. Since \lceil4+(b-1)/s\rceil\ge\lceil4+(b-1)/M\rceil, the stated constant is too small. For example, with b=10 and M=13, only s=1 represents M, which requires 13^{2\alpha}, whereas C_1(13,10) uses 5^{2\alpha}. A uniform constant needs s=1, i.e. (b+3)^{2\alpha}. In (iii), the per-M argument yields the stated c_1(n,b)=\frac{c_0}{2}6^{-\alpha} only for n\ge3(b-1). Cor:expDecay further drops the min with \ln(C_1)b^{-\alpha}, which is needed for n=b (Case 3) and for b=1. theo:Banach (ii),(iii) repeat the same s-versus-n pattern.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State (ii) with a uniform constant max{C_0 2^{\alpha+1}\gamma^{-2}(b+3)^{2\alpha},(b+2)^\alpha}, or give a refined argument for large n. For (iii), use (i) directly: \sigma_n\le C_1\exp(-\frac{c_0}{2}\lfloor(n-b+1)/2\rfloor^\alpha). Restate Cor:expDecay for n\ge3(b-1) with the min handled, and adjust the Banach analogues and remarks.
